top.title: AI, fake voter records raise new risks for 2027 elections
top.description: …Why media must not rush to publish election claims —Tech players By Juliet Umeh As Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general elections, voters may face a new kind of deception. The society is now rife with images, videos and audios that appear authentic but have been fabricated or altered. The concern has grown after the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it removed 1,609,553 records from the voters’ register following a technical assessment. The review examined suspected multiple registrations, unusual registration patterns, substituted photographs and irregularities linked to registration transactions. INEC also found cases in which some registration personnel deliberately bypassed established procedures, including provisions for exceptional circumstances involving persons with disabilities. The commission is investigating some flagged records. The findings have prompted questions about how the irregularities occurred and whether synthetic images or other AI-generated material could be used to undermine confidence in the electoral process. There is, however, no evidence in the material available that AI-generated images caused the irregularities in the register. Olaronke Alo of the BBC Disinformation Unit while speaking on Arise Television said its initial verification found that some of the images circulating online were present in the INEC register. She said: “What we did was to do the initial verification. We went into the INEC portal and began to trace some of the names and pictures being posted on social media. We found that these images were on the INEC register.” The unit also examined claims about inconsistent records, including one instance in which the same photograph appeared against different names. Alo said it found examples of apparently incomplete or unusual names and records alleged to belong to deceased people, including former President Muhammadu Buhari. She said the unit’s task was to verify claims circulating online, rather than assess whether INEC’s response was adequate. False claims can travel fast The risks extend beyond the voters’ register. top.description: Turmeric capsules are touted as remedies for joint problems olga Yastremska/Alamy Turmeric supplements seem to have little to no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis. That’s according to one of the most rigorous assessments of the evidence yet, which focused on four randomised controlled trials comparing the supplements to placebo pills. Osteoarthritis, which affects more than 500 million people worldwide , is caused by damage to cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, resulting in pain, stiffness and inflammation. Standard treatments include painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs that can ease symptoms. “But many people see little or no benefit,” says Philip Conaghan at the University of Leeds, UK, who wasn’t involved in the latest review. Read more There are only a few anti-ageing supplements that actually work Turmeric supplements are often touted as an alternative therapy. They contain curcumin, a compound that gives turmeric its yellow colour and is thought to have anti-inflammatory properties. Yet such beliefs are often based on prior flawed studies , says Ivan Shirinsky at the Research Institute of Internal and Preventive Medicine in Novosibirsk, Russia. Advertisement Shirinsky and his colleagues analysed results from four randomised controlled trials, collectively involving more than 370 participants with knee osteoarthritis. Participants were randomly assigned to take either a supplement containing turmeric extract or placebo pills two or three times per day, for between eight weeks and three months. Each trial used a slightly different supplement containing a different curcumin dose. “We looked at the most rigorous evidence available,” says Shirinsky. Among those who took a placebo, knee pain decreased by 1.6 points, on average, on a scale from 0 to 10 by the end of the study. Those taking turmeric supplements experienced an average 2.3-point decrease in pain, meaning the difference between the turmeric and placebo groups was half that required to be meaningful to patients based on prior studies , says Shirinsky. top.title: Innovator develops machine to reduce drudgery in post-harvest cleaning of farm
top.description: By Cynthia Alo The use of manual methods to sort and wash agricultural produce, including tigernuts, ginger, potatoes and grains, may become less demanding with the development of a locally made machine designed to integrate sorting, washing and drying operations. The innovation, developed by a Kogi State-born physicist and innovator, Kabir Umar, is aimed at addressing the labour-intensive and often unhygienic methods used by smallholder farmers, cleaning artisans and agro-processors to prepare agricultural commodities for local consumption and processing. Umar said the absence of affordable integrated cleaning equipment had left many small-scale operators dependent on manual sorting and washing, while those seeking mechanised alternatives often had to acquire expensive imported specialised equipment. He identified tigernuts as one of the commodities particularly affected by the challenge, explaining that some cleaning artisans still use their legs to wash the nuts before sorting them by hand. According to him, similar challenges affect the handling of other agricultural commodities, including ginger, potatoes, millet, beans and hibiscus flowers, popularly known as zobo. Umar said the idea for the machine emerged in 2020 after he ventured into agro-processing and encountered difficulties with the cleaning and drying of raw agricultural materials, which he identified as an important first step in value addition. He subsequently developed a multipurpose post-harvest sorting and washing machine, with an additional drying capability, designed to provide an integrated cleaning solution for different agricultural commodities. The innovator said he had mainly used the machine to sort and wash tigernuts for further processing into tigernut flour, adding that demonstrations to tigernut cleaning artisans showed its potential to reduce manual labour and improve productivity. He, however, disclosed that the machine was still at an advanced prototype stage and had yet to be deployed sustainably to support farmers and other operators across the agricultural value chain. According to him, wider adoption of the machine could improve the quality of agricultural produce entering local markets, support value addition, create jobs and strengthen the export potential of Nigerian commodities by improving their post-harvest handling. On the challenges facing the development, Umar identified inadequate funding as a major constraint that had slowed the transition from prototype development to commercial production. He expressed optimism that intervention through the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure’s (NASENI) Innovate Naija Challenge would help accelerate the commercialisation process. top.title: Summit to examine financing, market access for farmers, agribusinesses
top.description: By Cynthia Alo Farm financing, market access and innovative solutions for farmers and agribusiness operators will take centre stage at the fifth edition of the Wealth Creation Summit scheduled for November 28, 2026, in Abuja. The summit, organised by Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, is expected to bring together more than 1,000 farmers, agribusiness owners, investors, entrepreneurs and young Nigerians to explore opportunities for improving agricultural productivity and building sustainable businesses. The event, themed, “Unlocking Opportunities for Wealth Creation, Innovation and Sustainable Agricultural Development,” will focus on connecting agricultural producers and entrepreneurs with financing opportunities, markets, investors and business development support. A major feature of the summit will be the launch of the Wealth Creation Network, an agribusiness and entrepreneurship cooperative designed to support farmers, women and young entrepreneurs through training, access to agricultural inputs, produce aggregation, market linkages and business development services. The network is also expected to provide members with opportunities for bulk produce sales, export linkages and investment-readiness training. Speaking ahead of the event, Convener of the summit and Founder of Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, Uzua Brainz, said the initiative was intended to provide participants with practical opportunities beyond conference discussions. “We do not want people to attend Wealth Creation Summit 5.0, listen to speeches and return home exactly as they came. We want them to leave with clarity, structure, connections and practical opportunities for wealth creation,” he said. top.description: By Prince Osuagwu The growing intersection of technology, healthcare and e-commerce is opening new opportunities for mobile health delivery in Nigeria. This is as one of Nigeria’s composite e-commerce companies Konga attracted the partnership of global skincare brand, La Roche-Posay, to expand access to dermatological expertise and authentic skincare products in the country. The partnership, leverages Konga Health’s retail and e-commerce network to connect consumers with genuine dermatological products, professional skincare advice and health education. The partnership sealed in Lagos recently, demonstrated how technology-enabled retail platforms could complement conventional healthcare delivery by making specialist skincare products and information more accessible to consumers. La Roche-Posay, a brand under L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty, partnered with Konga Health, its official distributor in Nigeria, to promote dermatological science, product authenticity and informed skincare choices. A major attraction was the interactive skin science experience, which allowed visitors to explore common skin conditions, including hyperpigmentation, acne, damaged skin barriers, dryness and the effects of ultraviolet radiation. The programme also featured free consultations with certified dermatologists and members of the L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty MedSquad, who provided professional skin analysis, guidance and practical recommendations. Among the participating specialists were Dr Ayesha Akinkugbe, dermatologist and Vice-President of the Nigerian Association of Dermatologists, and Dr Folakemi Cole-Adeife. The event showcased five major La Roche-Posay product franchises: Cicaplast for skin repair, Mela B3 for hyperpigmentation, Anthelios for sun protection, Lipikar for dry and atopic-prone skin, and Effaclar for acne-prone skin. Speaking at the event, Leo Stan Ekeh, Chairman of Zinox Group, said the commercial opportunities in Nigeria’s beauty and personal-care market, was enormous. He added that the importance of bringing globally recognised brands and quality products closer to Nigerian consumers can never be overemphasised. For Anaïs Routhiau, Business Development Manager, LID LDB SSA, the Living Lab provided an opportunity to bring La Roche-Posay’s commitment to dermatological science closer to consumers, helping them better understand their skin and the science behind the products they use. nigeria.description: By Cynthia Alo The use of manual methods to sort and wash agricultural produce, including tigernuts, ginger, potatoes and grains, may become less demanding with the development of a locally made machine designed to integrate sorting, washing and drying operations. The innovation, developed by a Kogi State-born physicist and innovator, Kabir Umar, is aimed at addressing the labour-intensive and often unhygienic methods used by smallholder farmers, cleaning artisans and agro-processors to prepare agricultural commodities for local consumption and processing. Umar said the absence of affordable integrated cleaning equipment had left many small-scale operators dependent on manual sorting and washing, while those seeking mechanised alternatives often had to acquire expensive imported specialised equipment. He identified tigernuts as one of the commodities particularly affected by the challenge, explaining that some cleaning artisans still use their legs to wash the nuts before sorting them by hand. According to him, similar challenges affect the handling of other agricultural commodities, including ginger, potatoes, millet, beans and hibiscus flowers, popularly known as zobo. Umar said the idea for the machine emerged in 2020 after he ventured into agro-processing and encountered difficulties with the cleaning and drying of raw agricultural materials, which he identified as an important first step in value addition. He subsequently developed a multipurpose post-harvest sorting and washing machine, with an additional drying capability, designed to provide an integrated cleaning solution for different agricultural commodities. The innovator said he had mainly used the machine to sort and wash tigernuts for further processing into tigernut flour, adding that demonstrations to tigernut cleaning artisans showed its potential to reduce manual labour and improve productivity. He, however, disclosed that the machine was still at an advanced prototype stage and had yet to be deployed sustainably to support farmers and other operators across the agricultural value chain. According to him, wider adoption of the machine could improve the quality of agricultural produce entering local markets, support value addition, create jobs and strengthen the export potential of Nigerian commodities by improving their post-harvest handling. On the challenges facing the development, Umar identified inadequate funding as a major constraint that had slowed the transition from prototype development to commercial production. He expressed optimism that intervention through the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure’s (NASENI) Innovate Naija Challenge would help accelerate the commercialisation process. nigeria.title: Summit to examine financing, market access for farmers, agribusinesses
nigeria.description: By Cynthia Alo Farm financing, market access and innovative solutions for farmers and agribusiness operators will take centre stage at the fifth edition of the Wealth Creation Summit scheduled for November 28, 2026, in Abuja. The summit, organised by Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, is expected to bring together more than 1,000 farmers, agribusiness owners, investors, entrepreneurs and young Nigerians to explore opportunities for improving agricultural productivity and building sustainable businesses. The event, themed, “Unlocking Opportunities for Wealth Creation, Innovation and Sustainable Agricultural Development,” will focus on connecting agricultural producers and entrepreneurs with financing opportunities, markets, investors and business development support. A major feature of the summit will be the launch of the Wealth Creation Network, an agribusiness and entrepreneurship cooperative designed to support farmers, women and young entrepreneurs through training, access to agricultural inputs, produce aggregation, market linkages and business development services. The network is also expected to provide members with opportunities for bulk produce sales, export linkages and investment-readiness training. Speaking ahead of the event, Convener of the summit and Founder of Golden Harvest Acres Ventures, Uzua Brainz, said the initiative was intended to provide participants with practical opportunities beyond conference discussions. “We do not want people to attend Wealth Creation Summit 5.0, listen to speeches and return home exactly as they came. We want them to leave with clarity, structure, connections and practical opportunities for wealth creation,” he said. nigeria.description: By Prince Osuagwu The growing intersection of technology, healthcare and e-commerce is opening new opportunities for mobile health delivery in Nigeria. This is as one of Nigeria’s composite e-commerce companies Konga attracted the partnership of global skincare brand, La Roche-Posay, to expand access to dermatological expertise and authentic skincare products in the country. The partnership, leverages Konga Health’s retail and e-commerce network to connect consumers with genuine dermatological products, professional skincare advice and health education. The partnership sealed in Lagos recently, demonstrated how technology-enabled retail platforms could complement conventional healthcare delivery by making specialist skincare products and information more accessible to consumers. La Roche-Posay, a brand under L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty, partnered with Konga Health, its official distributor in Nigeria, to promote dermatological science, product authenticity and informed skincare choices. A major attraction was the interactive skin science experience, which allowed visitors to explore common skin conditions, including hyperpigmentation, acne, damaged skin barriers, dryness and the effects of ultraviolet radiation. The programme also featured free consultations with certified dermatologists and members of the L’Oréal Dermatological Beauty MedSquad, who provided professional skin analysis, guidance and practical recommendations. Among the participating specialists were Dr Ayesha Akinkugbe, dermatologist and Vice-President of the Nigerian Association of Dermatologists, and Dr Folakemi Cole-Adeife. Speaking at the event, Leo Stan Ekeh, Chairman of Zinox Group, said the commercial opportunities in Nigeria’s beauty and personal-care market, was enormous. He added that the importance of bringing globally recognised brands and quality products closer to Nigerian consumers can never be overemphasised. nigeria.description: … Warn of burnout, stroke risks, seek healthier work environments By Chioma Obinna Health experts yesterday expressed concerns that Nigerian medical doctors are exposing themselves to increased risks of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes, through excessive workloads, sleep deprivation, chronic stress and failure to undergo regular medical checks. The experts, who spoke at the Annual General Meeting/Scientific Conference of the Medical and Dental Consultants’ Association of Nigeria (MDCAN), Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Ebute-Metta, Lagos tagged: “ Your Body, Your Responsibility: A Personal Guide to Cancer Risk Reduction for Physicians, lamented that physicians, despite their knowledge of healthy living, often neglect their own health while attending to patients. They called for a deliberate shift towards preventive healthcare among doctors, warning that professional dedication should not come at the expense of their lives. Speaking at the conference, Chief Consultant Cardiologist at the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH, Dr Folashade Daniel, said doctors must consciously balance their professional responsibilities with adequate rest, exercise, healthy eating and routine medical examinations. Daniel, who spoke on protecting the hearts of physicians, said: “I don’t think physicians can balance their work, healthy living, and their mobility. It has to be intentional.” She noted that doctors sometimes work for extended hours, leaving little time for personal health, but stressed that they must make deliberate efforts to recover and maintain healthy lifestyles. “First of all, know that your life is not just, your life doesn’t just entail your job. You are a person, you have a family, and you have responsibilities. Yes, to your patients, but also to your family, to yourself,” she said. According to her, doctors should make adequate rest, relaxation, healthy eating and physical activity essential parts of their routines, rather than treating them as optional activities. She advised physicians with a family history of cardiovascular disease to exercise extra caution and make annual health checks a priority. “Take your birthday, for example, your one anniversary, to do a check-up. And then look up all the results with a colleague. Don’t just be your own doctors. Let somebody look at what you have, the results you have done, and give you advice as need arises,” Daniel said. The cardiologist also urged government to strengthen policies that promote healthier food choices and safer working environments. She identified excessive salt, preservatives and trans fats in food, particularly from repeatedly used frying oil, as concerns requiring stronger regulation. nigeria.title: Blindness: Eritrea, 10 others eliminate trachoma from Africa as Nigeria lags
nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe Eritrea has become the 11th country in the World Health Organisation (WHO) African Region to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem, raising hopes of ending a neglected tropical disease (NTD) that continues to threaten the sight of millions of people across the continent. The achievement, validated by WHO, places Eritrea among 11 African countries that have successfully tackled the disease through sustained public health interventions, improved access to treatment, hygiene promotion and community mobilisation. Eritrea joins Algeria, Benin, Burundi, Eritrea, The Gambia, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Mauritania, Senegal and Togo as the African countries that have received WHO validation as the number of countries that have achieved elimination globally stands at 34. Eritrea is also the 66th country globally and the 23rd in the WHO African Region to eliminate at least one neglected tropical disease. According to WHO, Eritrea achieved the milestone, following two decades of sustained interventions targeting the disease, particularly in remote rural communities where poor access to clean water, sanitation and healthcare had fuelled its spread. Eritrea’s success followed nationwide surveys conducted between 2006 and 2020, which helped identify affected communities and guide the rollout of interventions across the country. The government subsequently implemented WHO’s recommended SAFE strategy, a combination of surgery for advanced cases, antibiotics to clear infection, facial cleanliness to limit transmission and environmental improvements, particularly better access to water and sanitation. A notable feature of the campaign was its community-led sanitation approach, which delivered significant public health gains despite limited external funding. Health workers deployed digital tools for data collection and mapping to identify affected populations, track disease patterns and direct resources to hard-to-reach communities. In a congratulatory message, WHO Director-General, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said, “I congratulate the Government and people of Eritrea on this historic achievement. After two decades of determined effort, Eritrea has consigned trachoma as a public health problem to history. This is a victory for the communities most affected by this devastating disease, and a powerful example of what sustained national commitment can achieve.” On his part, WHO Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, said Eritrea’s achievement demonstrated the impact of political commitment, community participation and effective partnerships in tackling neglected tropical diseases. “I congratulate Eritrea on this historic public health milestone. nigeria.title: Eyesan seeks more opportunities for women in petroleum sector
nigeria.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Commission Chief Executive, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, has called for greater opportunities for women in the petroleum sector. Eyesan made the call on Wednesday while speaking on the topic, “Breaking Barriers,” at the 2026 Women in NNPC Limited (WIN) in Abuja, under the theme, “Powered by Her.” She asked women to also prioritise competence, resilience and continuous learning as critical tools for breaking barriers. A statement by the Commission said Eyesan urged women not to be discouraged by delayed promotions, stressing that professional growth requires patience, perseverance and commitment to excellence. Sharing her personal experience, Eyesan disclosed that she spent eight years in the same position without promotion but remained committed to her career. Eyesan also emphasised the importance of involving men in conversations about gender inclusion and women’s advancement, noting that some of the major milestones in her career were made possible by men who recognised her competence and provided opportunities. “I was appointed the first female Head of Strategy, not by a woman, but by a man who believed in my competence. I was also appointed as the first female EVP Upstream, NNPCL, by a man who believed in my competence, and today I stand as the first female CCE of NUPRC by Mr President, who is a man who believes that I will deliver,” she said. Acknowledging the gradual increase in opportunities for women in the industry, the NUPRC boss called for more deliberate efforts to achieve meaningful representation, advocating at least 25 per cent participation of women in leadership and decision-making positions. “Is it happening at the scale we want? Not quite, we need more. At least one in four. Not just because we want to make up the numbers but because we think we bring value to the table,” she said. The NUPRC boss also commended the Group Chief Executive Officer of NNPC Limited, Mr Bayo Ojulari, for the WIN initiative, describing it as a valuable platform for positioning young women for greater opportunities and leadership roles in the oil and gas industry. She noted that the Nigerian oil and gas industry was recording significant progress through collaboration between the regulator, NNPC Limited and other industry operators. nigeria.title: American strategist denies receiving $4.5m for Tinubu interview
nigeria.description: By Nwafor Sunday Polycarp, Online News Editor American political strategist and media personality, Diana London, has denied receiving $4.5 million from the Nigerian government for her recent interview with President Bola Tinubu. London, in a post on her X account on Wednesday night, described the allegation as a smear campaign, insisting that neither the Nigerian government nor anyone else in the country paid her the reported sum. She said her visit to Nigeria was to interview Tinubu for a documentary and to see the country for herself. “I unequivocally deny the claim that Nigeria’s government nor anyone else in Nigeria paid me $4.5 million. I went to Nigeria to interview President Tinubu @officialABAT for parts of a documentary and see Nigeria for myself. “This SMEAR CAMPAIGN can make noise, but can’t change the facts or stop me from speaking the truth,” she wrote. The denial comes amid controversy surrounding her interview with Tinubu at the Presidential Villa, Abuja, on Tuesday, and reports alleging that she was linked to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving the Nigerian government in the United States. Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar had called on the Presidency to clarify whether the interview was connected to the reported lobbying contract and disclose the details of the arrangement. In a statement issued on Wednesday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said US filings identified London as a consultant to DCI Group AZ, a firm reportedly engaged by the Nigerian government through Aster Legal. He said the filings indicated that DCI Group received a $4.5 million retainer but maintained that the Presidency should clarify whether the interview formed part of the contract. Atiku demanded the publication of the contract, details of the payment and the release of the full, unedited recording of the interview. He also questioned the nature of the engagement, arguing that the Presidency should establish whether the encounter was an independent journalistic exercise or part of a government-funded publicity arrangement. The former vice president further asked the government to disclose who authorised the payment, the source of the funds and whether public money was involved. The controversy followed London’s earlier social media posts praising the security partnership between Nigeria and the United States under Tinubu and US President Donald Trump. In one of the posts, she described Nigeria as the United States’ greatest ally in Africa, saying the security cooperation between both countries was producing results and could create further economic and trade opportunities. She also expressed appreciation for the opportunity to work with individuals representing Nigeria in efforts to strengthen relations between the Trump administration and the Nigerian government. nigeria.title: [VIDEO] Tinubu Can’t Alter State Police Bill, He’ll Definitely Sign It — Omole
nigeria.description: Lawyer and author Charles Omole has said that he does not expect President Bola Tinubu to make an alteration to the National Policing Bill transmitted to him by the National Assembly. Omole, who stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday. He explained that altering the bill would return the process to the Senate, House of Representatives and state houses of assembly for their approval. Omole noted further that the constitutional amendment is not the meat and bone of policing but simply allows state police to exist, while the National Policing Bill specifies the structure and functions of the state police. He, however, said that the National Policing Bill could not be considered until the constitutional amendment had gone through. He explained that while the 36 states would have their own police service, the police in the Federal Capital Territory would be under the control of the federal police service. Omole, however, said that part of the recommendation under the bill is that states cannot buy their own arms and ammunition at will. nigeria.title: Plateau 2027: PDP’s Scores Gov Mutfwang 15-20% In Performance
nigeria.description: The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Kephas Ropshik, on Wednesday said that Governor Caleb Mutfwang performed poorly in governance in the state. Ropshik, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , said the governor had not scored more than 20 per cent in performance. The PDP candidate said that leadership should be about performance and about the people. “In fact, I can tell you on a scale of one to 100, you can give him like 15 to 20 per cent in performance,” he said. “He still remains someone that I respect, but of course that, completely, is different from politics.” ﻿ He alleged that the governor defected to the All Progressives Congress (APC) when he could not cope with the crisis in the PDP. He, however, said that the governor did not leave with up to 15 per cent of the members of the PDP, insisting that Plateau is a PDP state. “You know, a man’s strength and leadership qualities are being tested when there are crises, but the governor couldn’t stand the crisis. He left for APC, and so there was an opening in the PDP to contest for governorship because, of course, the truth is this. Plateau has been a PDP state. “You can’t take that away from Plateau State, right? And so there was a vacancy, and so somebody needed to fill in the gap. And so even with the crisis, we believed in the PDP,” the candidate said. “Mutfwang did not live with 15, 20 per cent of people, I mean, in PDP to APC. The people, in fact, not even 10 per cent, because the people that followed him to APC are his appointees, and that’s the truth. “Ninety per cent of people on the Plateau still believe in the PDP.” Ropshik said that Plateau is one of the frontrunners in the Rainbow Coalition. He also said that he was working for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu. business.title: Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Scattered Spider Hacker Gets Six Years for $11.6 Million Crypto Theft A Scottish hacker tied to the Scattered Spider group was sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison on Tuesday for a text-message phishing and SIM-swapping scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Central District of California said . Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, received a 72-month sentence from U.S. District Judge John W. Holcomb in Santa Ana. He had pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. A restitution hearing is set for Dec. 11. Prosecutors did not say which cryptocurrencies were taken, and the release does not break the haul down by coin. Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, closing out a prosecution of a hacker crew that the Justice Department charged together. How the scheme worked From September 2021 to April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen companies, prosecutors said. The messages posed as the employer or one of its IT contractors and linked to fake login pages that captured usernames, passwords and other personal information. The group then used the stolen data to run SIM swaps, which move a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the attacker controls. That gave them a way into victims’ virtual currency accounts and wallets. The BBC reported that Buchanan set up a Telegram bot to collect the credentials as workers handed them over. The largest single theft, according to prosecutors, was $1.67 million taken from one victim in December 2022. Prosecutors said the thefts had “severe, life-altering consequences” for victims. The BBC said the money came from individual victims rather than from the companies whose employees were phished. Prosecutors first put the hacker group’s take at about $8 million, and the $11.6 million figure is the loss authorities calculated for the full scheme. From Scotland to a California courtroom Police Scotland searched Buchanan’s bedroom in April 2023 after a request from the FBI, the BBC said . Investigators found a device holding the names and addresses of victims, along with crypto seed phrases and account credentials belonging to at least one victim. Buchanan left the U.K. the following month. Spanish authorities arrested him at Palma de Mallorca Airport in 2024 as he tried to board a private flight to Naples. Bloomberg News reported, and Reuters relayed , that he was extradited from Spain in April 2025. He was charged with wire fraud and aggravated identity theft alongside four other alleged Scattered Spider members, and he has been in U.S. custody since. business.title: Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says It Won Court Order to Recover Frozen Hack Funds Binance says it has secured a court order from Abu Dhabi Global Market to help it recover crypto frozen after the record $6.3 billion hack last month, Reuters reported on Wednesday. The exchange has not said how much of the money the order covers. Reuters described Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM) as Binance’s main financial regulator. Binance deputy general counsel Dugan Bliss confirmed the order in a statement but gave no details on its terms. Neither the company nor Reuters said which assets it applies to. “We will continue using every lawful tool available to trace, freeze and recover stolen assets, support our partners in returning funds where possible, and keep those assets out of the hands of the attackers,” Bliss said. What is frozen Binance has said about $2.85 billion of the stolen tokens were frozen or intercepted after the Oct. 29 attack, according to its own incident report . That is roughly 45% of the $6.34 billion it says was affected. Most of it sits with stablecoin issuers. Tether said it froze more than $1.5 billion in USDT within 30 minutes of the attack, and Circle said it froze about $1.1 billion in USDC in coordination with law enforcement. Circle added that it does not decide who owns frozen assets, a question it left to law enforcement and the courts. The Justice Department has separately obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of the stolen crypto. It is part of more than $2.7 billion that Justice says government and private-sector efforts have frozen. Criminal Division head A. Tysen Duva said the department helped “immediately halt about half of this historic breach.” Reuters did not say how the ADGM order fits with the U.S. action. How the hack unfolded Binance says the attack began months earlier, with a tampered software installer that compromised one engineer in June. In September, another engineer was approached by a fake recruiter and persuaded to run a bogus interview assignment that installed malware, the company said. From there, the attackers reached an internal wallet-signing service and drained Binance hot wallets across multiple blockchains on Oct. 29. The thefts included 233.46 million XRP, about 970,500 SOL and 18,270 BTC, according to Binance. The FBI has attributed the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, and Binance has said the same. Pyongyang denies involvement. Blockchain analysts said the attacker tried to outrun the freezes by swapping stablecoins into ether over about 20 minutes, but the issuers moved faster. That split matters for bitcoin. Tether and Circle can block their own tokens, but bitcoin has no issuer. The stolen BTC is not covered by those freezes and can be stopped only if it reaches an exchange or service that blocks it. Dr. Olowolafe said Ikogosi’s task now is to give visitors compelling reasons to come, stay longer and spend across local businesses. He pointed to the recent Ikogosi 17.5km Race, which drew runners from across Nigeria alongside athletes from Ghana, Kenya and Ethiopia, as an example of what happens when private initiative meets local hospitality. He urged the same thinking for lifestyle and executive tourism, with the ambition of making Ikogosi a premier international destination for weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate retreats and landmark gatherings. “Our natural landscape will draw people in. entertainment.title: Miss Universe 2026: Meet the 17 African Queens Representing the Continent
entertainment.description: From left: Miss Universe Democratic Republic of the Congo 2026 Jessi Kalambayi, Miss Universe Namibia 2026 Charene Labuschagne, and Miss Universe Botswana 2026 Dabilo Moses ahead of the 75th Miss Universe finale in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Miss Universe stage is getting a beautiful dose of African representation this year, with 17 contestants from across the continent making their way to Puerto Rico for the pageant’s 75th edition. And there are plenty of stories to discover among them, from Uganda ’s historic debut to Nigeria ’s Danielle Adewusi , whose journey to the competition comes with a lovely family connection. Taking place in San Juan, Puerto Rico, the Diamond Anniversary edition will bring together 116 contestants from around the world, all hoping to claim the newly unveiled 75th-anniversary crown, The Radiance of an Eternal Legacy. The grand finale is scheduled for Tuesday, 24 November 2026, at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum. This year’s show will be hosted by R’Bonney Gabriel , Mario Lopez , Zuri Hall and Dayanara Torres . At the end of the night, reigning Miss Universe 2025 Fátima Bosch of Mexico will pass on her crown to a new winner. Bosch took the title in Thailand last November, ahead of contestants from Thailand, Venezuela, the Philippines and Côte d’Ivoire. For Africa, the road to this year’s competition has come with a few changes. Angola, the Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, Zambia and Zimbabwe were unable to participate due to U.S. travel and visa restrictions, while Côte d’Ivoire, Mauritius, Rwanda and Senegal withdrew from the competition. Still, 17 African countries have contestants in the running, including Uganda, which is making its historic Miss Universe debut. Cameroon, Ethiopia, Kenya, Sierra Leone and Tunisia are among the countries returning to the global stage. Representing Nigeria is 29-year-old medical doctor and women’s health advocate Danielle Adewusi, also known as Danielle Fadeke Adewusi. Her participation adds a special family detail to the story: she won Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 in Lagos, 35 years after her mother, Tonia Okogbenin , represented the country at Miss Universe 1991. From first-time participation to familiar faces returning to the competition, these are the 17 African beauty queens representing the continent at Miss Universe 2026. Dabilo Moses — Botswana Representing Botswana is 26-year-old Dabilo Moses from Gaborone (born in Tutume). entertainment.title: Beyoncé Becomes First Artist in Grammy History to Earn 100 Nominations!
entertainment.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . Now all eyes turn to Sunday, 7 February 2027, when the 2027 Grammy Awards take place at the Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles and we find out whether nomination number 100 turns into Grammy win number 36. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. It also caps off an extraordinary 2026 for his legacy, coming just months after the Recording Academy presented him with a posthumous Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in February, another first for an African artist. From left, Made Kuti, Femi Kuti, Yeni Kuti, and Seun Kuti in Los Angeles for Fela Aníkúlápó Kuti’s posthumous induction into the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Photo Credit: Femi Kuti/Instagram Representing the Afrobeat legend on the night were members of the Kuti family, with his children Yeni Kuti , Femi Kuti , Seun Kuti , and Shalewa Kuti , alongside his grandson Made Kuti , stepping out in Los Angeles to accept the honour on his behalf. Speaking on the milestone, the family reflected on how remarkable it is to see Fela receive both the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award and a Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction in the very same year. Meanwhile, Sade Adu —born Helen Folasade Adu in Ibadan—was inducted in th e Performer category as the frontwoman of her acclaimed British band Sade , alongside longtime bandmates Stuart Matthewman , Paul Spencer Denman , and Andrew Hale . Earning their spot on their second nomination, the group behind timeless soul-jazz records such as “Smooth Operator”, “The Sweetest Taboo”, and “Your Love Is King” opted to sit out the ceremony in true low-key fashion, though they shared a warm message thanking fans and dedicating the milestone to their late longtime producer Mike Pela . technology.title: Anthropic decides to go head-to-head with GTA VI release, schedules IPO for the same day
technology.description: Well, it’s official: Anthropic will become the first publicly-traded frontier AI lab in history come the opening of markets on Thursday. The company kicked off its IPO roadshow last week, announcing plans to offer 825 million shares with an IPO price between $70 and $78 a share when sales begin Thursday. The company's most recent SEC filing cites that price range but allows for the possibility of a higher price, which should be determined Wednesday night. Late on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported that Anthropic would price at $83, citing people familiar. Whatever the case, Anthropic is likely to be valued at more than $1 trillion. Anthropic’s debutante ball has been on the horizon for a while, and documents leaked in late September made it all the more inevitable as the company’s finances revved up and it sought to capture the momentum of its best quarter to date before things start to tail off. The company revised its IPO documents on November 2, warning that the 12x growth it was touting was unlikely to continue in the long term due to compute infrastructure investments to the tune of nearly $900 billion it was on the hook for over the next few years. "In the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our revenue was $33.2 billion, representing a year-over-year growth rate of 1,206%," the revised prospectus reads. "We do not expect our revenue will continue to grow at comparable rates, and we cannot assure you that it will continue to grow at all." It’s possible, in other words, that Anthropic may never be a money maker despite the hype and its position as the first mover. The IPO prospectus is short on answers to critical questions and leaves a lot unanswered - like, for example, whether it’s going to actually be able to pay its bills. "Our ability to meet the substantial and growing financial obligations of these requirements to secure compute depends on our ability to generate significant revenue growth," the updated prospectus admits. Investors don’t seem to care right now, though. Anthropic already has compute commitments amounting to roughly $70.7 billion in the next 12 months. That’s just shy of its $81 billion run-rate as of October 31. Expect more hot air to be injected tomorrow, adding additional surface tension and the possibility of even more losses if, and when, this monster pops. ®

technology.description: Hot on the heels of serious vulnerabilities in seemingly every other widely used software powering the entire internet, F5 today released emergency patches for 10 bugs in open source NGINX. These include critical remote code execution flaws that let attackers hijack NGINX servers with HTTP/2 enabled, as well as the millions of websites running NGINX, to steal sensitive data and disrupt services. “At this time, we have found no evidence of active exploitation of any of these vulnerabilities in the wild,” and F5 spokesperson told The Register . “We continue to monitor closely and will share updates via myF5 as we learn more.” As with all of the other recently disclosed vulnerabilities in foundational technologies like PHP, Apache, and Java, these critical NGINX bugs were uncovered by researchers using AI. One of them has been hiding in the code for at least 10 years. Tomer Schwartz, Wiz’s chief technology officer of exposure management and AppSec, helped find the bug, along with researchers from Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint working independently. Schwartz told The Register that this wave of AI-discovered flaws “point to a new reality.” “We need to treat every internet-connected system as potentially vulnerable,” Schwartz said. “AI has changed not only which vulnerabilities can be found, but how quickly longstanding risks can become real threats.” NGINX is the world’s most widely used open source web server, handling HTTPS requests and routing incoming traffic to the right application or API. It powers about a third of all websites (around 225 million ), and F5 maintains the open source version. On Wednesday, F5 published an out-of-band security notification that addressed 10 CVEs in open source NGINIX. If you run NGINX, update to 1.31.9 as soon as possible. CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 Two of the vulns are especially serious as they allow a remote attacker to execute code on the NGINX server without authentication. These two, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 , both received a critical, 9.2 CVSS rating, and CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. All of the security shops listed earlier independently found at least one of these two CVEs - most, if not all, with an AI assist - and reported them to F5. “Both vulnerabilities are memory-safety issues in how NGINX handles HTTP/2 traffic,” Schwartz and fellow Wiz kid Nir Ohfeld said in a Wednesday blog about the two bugs. “In CVE-2026-123633, a connection's memory is freed while a request still needs it, creating a use-after-free. technology.title: To rank the world's biggest supercomputers, we're gonna need a bigger bench
technology.description: For decades, the Top500 list has tirelessly ranked the world’s biggest, most powerful, and often most unique publicly-known supercomputers. With the rise of generative AI, the list no longer lives up to its name. China’s Lineshine supercomputer at 2.2 exaFLOPS of double precision compute in the High-Performance Linpack (HPL) benchmark may be the top system on the bi-annual ranking, but it’s nowhere near the biggest compute cluster in the world. Superclusters like SpaceXAI’s Colossus, Meta’s Promethius, and OpenAI’s Stargate pack hundreds of thousands of GPUs, dwarfing anything on the Top500 today. “These [companies] are not interested in submitting to the Top500,” Eth Zürich’s Torsten Hoefler said during his Supercomputing address this week. It’s a dilemma that the founders of the Top500 ranking are now grappling with. And some believe it may be time for a rethink. “What’s really needed for tracking that more appropriately is not just a different benchmark but also different methodology,” Top500 author Erich Strohmaier said. For a long time, Strohmaier explains, compute capability was roughly aligned with capacity. What happened in the last few years with AI is “capacity really pulled ahead of capability in terms of market size,” he said. “We were and we still are very focused on capability.” By capability, Strohmaier is referring to the ability to run one code across the entire cluster. “Our prime rule for benchmarking is, you have to benchmark your whole system with one code and you cannot just add two parts up to make up a number,” he explained. This is problematic for the large clusters major hyperscalers and cloud providers are now building to fuel the AI boom. “All those systems are capacity systems,” Strohmaier said. They’re not designed to run one piece of code but have instead been architected to run many, many smaller or medium-sized code instantiations, which may include training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and of course inference. Because of this, Strohmaier says, it wouldn’t be reasonable to expect SpaceXAI to run something High-Performance Linpack (HPL) on a cluster like Colossus. But these clusters are still worth tracking. They'll just need a new benchmark better suited to judging the capability of these arrays while at the same time preventing operators from gaming the system. What shape or form such a benchmark might take remains to be seen. Developing a new benchmark or methodology is no small task, and changing the existing benchmarks isn’t ideal. ”If we do anything to the benchmark itself, we’re going to lose the historic trends, which is extremely valuable,” Hoefler said. Allowing for lower precisions — HPL-MxP already does this to some extent — is one avenue for addressing the fact that these accelerators are increasingly trading FP64 performance for lower-accuracy floating-point data types like FP8 or FP4. science.title: Turmeric supplements offer little benefit for knee osteoarthritis
science.description: Turmeric capsules are touted as remedies for joint problems olga Yastremska/Alamy Turmeric supplements seem to have little to no effect on pain and mobility problems caused by knee osteoarthritis. That’s according to one of the most rigorous assessments of the evidence yet, which focused on four randomised controlled trials comparing the supplements to placebo pills. Osteoarthritis, which affects more than 500 million people worldwide , is caused by damage to cartilage that cushions the ends of bones, resulting in pain, stiffness and inflammation. Standard treatments include painkillers and anti-inflammatory drugs that can ease symptoms. “But many people see little or no benefit,” says Philip Conaghan at the University of Leeds, UK, who wasn’t involved in the latest review. Read more There are only a few anti-ageing supplements that actually work Turmeric supplements are often touted as an alternative therapy. They contain curcumin, a compound that gives turmeric its yellow colour and is thought to have anti-inflammatory properties. Yet such beliefs are often based on prior flawed studies , says Ivan Shirinsky at the Research Institute of Internal and Preventive Medicine in Novosibirsk, Russia. Advertisement Shirinsky and his colleagues analysed results from four randomised controlled trials, collectively involving more than 370 participants with knee osteoarthritis. Participants were randomly assigned to take either a supplement containing turmeric extract or placebo pills two or three times per day, for between eight weeks and three months. Each trial used a slightly different supplement containing a different curcumin dose. “We looked at the most rigorous evidence available,” says Shirinsky. Among those who took a placebo, knee pain decreased by 1.6 points, on average, on a scale from 0 to 10 by the end of the study. Those taking turmeric supplements experienced an average 2.3-point decrease in pain, meaning the difference between the turmeric and placebo groups was half that required to be meaningful to patients based on prior studies , says Shirinsky. science.description: null Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean. We need sensitive telescopes monitoring the sky for a long time in order to catch this effect." In December 2025, observations from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope provided the final evidence that allowed researchers to fully reconstruct what happened before, during, and after the merger of a binary star system nicknamed Bao in the Andromeda galaxy. (Image credit: Image: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, Viraj Karambelkar (Columbia), Kishalay De (Columbia); Image Processing: Alyssa Pagan (STScI); Acknowledgment: DSS, Robert Gendler) In the new study, the researchers investigated a red giant star designated WNTR23bzdiq, which is located about 2.5 million light-years away in the Andromeda galaxy . The star is about seven times heftier and 350 times wider than our own sun . In 2023, using NASA's now-defunct NEOWISE space telescope and the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory in California, the scientists noticed that this star was brightening. By analyzing previous records, they found that the red giant had gradually started growing more luminous in 2018. The researchers had previously suggested this brightening potentially occurred because the giant star engulfed a companion star. As this companion spiraled toward the giant's core, it would generate friction, heat and light, explaining the increasing luminosity. Then, near the end of 2025, the astronomers saw a giant eruption of light from this giant star. NASA's James Webb Space Telescope observed the star just 47 days after that eruption, allowing the team to characterize the event in detail. The researchers now propose that this explosion happened when a companion star about 70% the sun's mass rammed into the giant's heart. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
science.description: null On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere. Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere once kept Mars warm enough to sustain liquid water on its surface , and losing that greenhouse gas turned Mars into a cold and dry place. An Atlas V rocket launches NASA's Mars MAVEN orbiter into space from Florida's Cape Canaveral Space Force Base on Nov. 18, 2013. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) Why it mattered NASA's MAVEN spacecraft was the first Mars orbiter ever built to measure how the Martian atmosphere interacts with solar wind , as well as how that constant stream of particles from the sun slowly stripped the Red Planet of its precious atmosphere over time. After its launch in 2013, MAVEN spent about 10 months en route to Mars before entering orbit on Sept. 21, 2014 . The spacecraft then spent the better part of 11 years studying the Red Planet from orbit using three different suites of instruments: An imaging ultraviolet spectrograph to study the global characteristics of the Martian atmosphere; a Neutral Gas and Ion Mass Spectromenter to measure its composition; and a six-instrument setup to study how Mars' ionosphere reacts to solar wind. An artist's view of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft at Mars on a mission to study its upper atmosphere. (Image credit: NASA) "The science MAVEN has given us is key to informing what kind of radiation protection and safety measures we must take before sending humans to Mars," Louise Prockter, NASA director of planetary science, said in June 2026 after the mission concluded. "The data collected from MAVEN will continue to provide valuable insight into Mars for decades to come." MAVEN was originally designed to study Mars for 1 full Earth year after arriving at the Red Planet. That mission ended in 2016, but the spacecraft managed to survive for another 10 years adding more observations for scientists to study. NASA ultimately began using MAVEN as a communications relay for other missions at Mars as the orbiter aged. In December 2025, MAVEN went silent , with NASA losing communication with the orbiter. science.title: Earth is missing over a billion years of geological history. Scientists may have discovered why
science.description: null More than a billion years of Earth's history has seemingly vanished. Across the planet, ancient rock formations contain colossal gaps in the geological record, leaving scientists puzzled over what happened to the missing chapters of our planet's past. Now, researchers believe they may have found an explanation, and the answer lies deep inside Earth . Normally, layers of sediment build up over time, eventually forming sedimentary rocks that preserve clues about our planet's past. Older layers generally lie beneath younger ones, allowing geologists to reconstruct ancient environments and understand how Earth has changed over billions of years. But the geological record isn't always so neatly arranged. In the Grand Canyon, rock layers separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, revealing a vast gap in Earth's geological record. (Image credit: Marcia Straub via Getty Images) One of the most striking examples is found in the Grand Canyon, where rocks separated by hundreds of millions of years sit directly on top of one another, as if some force or phenomenon removed the layers that geologists would expect to see in between. This enormous gap in Earth's geological timeline is part of the phenomenon known as the Great Unconformity. It's not just the Grand Canyon. Similar gaps have been identified across Europe, Australia, Africa and Asia. Depending on the location, the missing interval ranges from approximately 200 million years to more than a billion years. "Imagine a book where a huge section in the middle has been ripped out," study lead author Santosh Dhungana said in a statement . "The Great Unconformity is that gap in Earth's story, with the narrative jumping from the early chapters straight to a much later part of the story. Our research suggests these pages weren't lost by chance." The Great Unconformity imaged here shows 550 million year old Tapeats Sandstone resting on 1.7 billion year old Vishnu Schist, in Blacktail Canyon along the Colorado River in Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. (Image credit: William Dummitt via Getty Images) What erased the geological record? In a new study published in the journal Nature, Dhungana and study co-author Nicolas Flament investigated whether activity far below Earth's surface was to blame. Using computer models, they explored how the slow circulation of hot rock within Earth's mantle may have affected the continents over hundreds of millions of years. Murphy (Wyle Information Systems, LLC) NASA launched a new competition inviting U.S. companies to produce prototypes of mid-power Hall effect thrusters – a type of electric propulsion system considered crucial for future space operations and exploration. Hall effect thrusters use an electric field to accelerate a propellant gas, producing efficient thrust for long-duration missions. Used for propelling satellites and deep space robotic vehicles, Hall effect thruster systems are critical technology. NASA’s Advanced Mid-Power Electric Rocket (AMPERE) Challenge is offering $500,000, split between two winning U.S. companies, to accelerate the maturation of mid-power systems that could be foundational to supporting future NASA and commercial missions. science.title: New Scientist is 70 years old – join us in celebrating
science.description: Julianna Funk/Alamy Break open the bubbly, light the candles and get ready to party – New Scientist is 70 years old! Times have certainly changed since we published our first issue in 1956. Back then, some scientists had proposed that our carbon dioxide emissions were warming the planet, but the idea was controversial. Biologists were only beginning to unpick how DNA, whose structure had just been elucidated by Francis Crick, James Watson, Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, encoded the instructions for building organisms. The founders of this magazine couldn’t have envisaged the many ways that the web and smartphones would change daily life. We are even old enough that what once seemed futuristic is now pleasantly quaint. Launching our first website, Planet Science , in 1995, we declared that, “As the technologies mature, quite soon and at a terminal near you, it may be possible to hear interviews with well-known scientists”. Our digital offering has expanded greatly since then, with these sorts of interviews now available across our podcast and video channels. That said, we also speculated that it might be possible to “manipulate three-dimensional models of molecules” on a future version of our website, which we still haven’t quite managed to deliver. To mark our anniversary, we have put together a timeline of the biggest breakthroughs of the past 70 years . I enjoyed diving into our archives in search of how we reported era-defining moments. Our assessments haven’t always been on the money: after Yuri Gagarin’s space flight in 1961, for example, our correspondent declared “it is almost physically impossible for [the US] to beat the Russians to the moon”. Advertisement The secret to New Scientist ‘s longevity is a devoted following of readers A clear demonstration, if one were needed, that most predictions turn out to be wrong. But looking ahead is in New Scientist ‘s DNA, so, bravely – or foolishly – we press on. The main feature in this special issue is a trip to the year 2096, seven decades from now, for an imagined article for our 140th anniversary . To make our predictions as informed as possible, Jacob Aron consulted a panoply of scientists for their views and wove it all together to create one plausible path for the future . Sometimes, it turns out that fiction writers can see the future more accurately than scientists. Emily H. Wilson has trawled through 70 years of sci-fi in search of the most prescient predictions . Robert A. Heinlein, Ursula K. Le Guin, Octavia E. Butler and Cixin Liu are among those who have shown remarkable foresight. Of course, the secret to New Scientist’s longevity is a devoted following who have been with us since the days of Daedalus, Enigma and Grimbledon Down. science.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Past times That creaking sound you just heard was Feedback’s ageing joints as we painfully sat down to type out this commemorative column. We have been here for a considerable number of decades, to the point that our recollection of our earliest missives has become faded and confused. Indeed, Feedback’s history is long and storied, to the point that it would defy the efforts of even the most conscientious biographer. We have been through many incarnations, most of whom went on to do far more felicitous things with their lives. It is a little-discussed fact, one not even known to reality, that a previous Feedback helped David Foster Wallace out by composing Infinite Jest over the course of a bank holiday weekend. We’re told that former Feedbacks also secretly performed the guitar solos on Stairway to Heaven and Killing in the Name . Advertisement For these reasons, most incarnations of Feedback were and are anonymous. Indeed, the identity of the current Feedback is known only to the king, the prime minister and the head of MI5. This anonymity has its drawbacks: our collective memory only stretches back so far. Thankfully, our editor took it upon themselves to venture into the New Scientist archive, in search of the first Feedbacks. It is difficult to fully convey what the archive is like, but if you imagine the warehouse at the end of Raiders of the Lost Ark and then insert a leaking roof and a surfeit of rats, your mental image will not be too badly astray. Escaping with only a minor amputation and an urgent need to be vaccinated, the editor delivered to us pages from the very first New Scientist . science.title: Are these the most spectacular and intriguing beetles in the world?
science.description: The glorious flower chafer Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum What animal is older than the dinosaurs and accounts for nearly a quarter of species on Earth? It is the magnificent beetle, an insect whose wings rest underneath a hard, protective case that often displays beautiful colours and intricate ornaments. “Wherever you stand on the land surface of the Earth save only for Antarctica, you are never more than a few metres from a beetle,” writes Maxwell Barclay in Interesting Beetles , which showcases some of their stunning variety. The main image shows the glorious flower chafer ( Howdenypa gloriosa ), a stunning opalescent green and blue. Its sleek flight from flower to flower, which takes place with the wing cases closed, unlike the clumsier flights of beetles with open wing cases, has attracted attention from aerospace engineers. They have fitted some flower chafers with tiny wireless transmitters to better understand how they manoeuvre while flying. Below is the Colorado potato beetle ( Leptinotarsa decemlineata ), which has a destructive relationship with humans. After the potato was introduced to North America, this striped beetle started to prefer spuds to native foods and quickly became a worldwide pest. Advertisement The Colorado potato beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Below, the carbuncle frog-legged beetle ( Sagra carbunculus ) shows off the buff hind legs that earned it its amphibian-inspired name and serve it well in battle – or when competing for an iridescent mate. The carbuncle frog-legged beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum The specimens in these images are taken from the archives of the Natural History Museum in London, where Barclay is senior curator in charge of beetles. It was difficult, he writes in his book, to choose which to include, “because each of the 400,000 beetle species has an interesting story to tell”. The violin beetle ( Mormolyce phyllodes ) shown below makes up for being an inelegant flyer by having a unique body shape that allows it to blend in with fallen leaves and winged seeds of trees in the steamy tropical rainforests where it resides. The violin beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Finally, the desert fog-basking beetle ( Onymacris bicolor ) shown below is another master of adaptation that can survive in places as arid and harsh as the Namib desert in southern Africa. Elegant in its black-and-white garb, this insect climbs to the top of a dune when conditions are right, points its head down and waits for dew to condense on special structures on its wings and then run into its mouth, keeping it alive. The desert fog-basking beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Barclay writes that beetles can not only survive in all these habitats, from potato fields to tropical forests and deserts, but that they are an integral part of each of them. science.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
science.description: null United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own issues at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28 , and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.) ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's update. Vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit. In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance. Vulcan Centaur rises into the sky on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure. Vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.
